statement: For the parametric curve $x=t^{2}$, $y=t^{3}-3t$, find $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ and the coordinates of the stationary points.
solution: $\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{dy/dt}{dx/dt}=\frac{3t^{2}-3}{2t}$. Stationary points occur when $\frac{dy}{dx}=0$, i.e. $3t^{2}-3=0$, so $t=\pm1$. At $t=1$: $(x,y)=(1,-2)$. At $t=-1$: $(x,y)=(1,2)$. The stationary points are $(1,-2)$ and $(1,2)$.
hints: Differentiate x and y with respect to t.
Set the numerator to zero and find t.
